html:
The Union of Transylvania with Romania was declared at a great assembly of Romanians in Alba Iulia on 1 December 1918, as Austria-Hungary broke up at the end of World War I.

Romanians were the largest group in Transylvania, which had been part of Hungary for centuries. Bessarabia had joined Romania earlier in 1918 and Bukovina in November, so the country doubled in size into Greater Romania. The Treaty of Trianon confirmed the new border in 1920. Hungarians, now a large minority, saw it as a loss. King Ferdinand and Queen Marie were crowned at Alba Iulia in 1922. Romania lost northern Transylvania to Hungary in 1940 but regained it after World War II. 1 December is Romania's national day.
sum: The Union of Transylvania with Romania was declared at a great assembly of Romanians in Alba Iulia on 1 December 1918, as Austria-Hungary broke up at the end of World War I.
